archetype.name: Gunslinger (play-extender)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who will hold the ball to extend a play, either with his legs or by taking a shot. His career has swung from top-10 efficiency to bottom-third depending on how well that gamble is protected and timed.

report.headline: Sacks, not accuracy, buried his 0-3 start; the thumb is now the question
report.take:
Mayfield's career is a series of swings. He posted a 0.207 EPA a play and 41 touchdowns in 2024, then fell back to a middling 0.089 last year. Through the whole run he has been the same type of player: he holds the ball, hunts for something better, scrambles well and accepts sacks and interceptions as the cost. His pressure-to-sack rate has sat in the high 30s for three straight seasons, so the sack habit is not new. What is new is how badly it went in three games before a dislocated thumb put Jalon Daniels under center for weeks 4 through 6.

The raw line looks awful: -0.274 EPA per dropback, 42nd of 45, on an 0-3 record. Look at what produced it. He converted 44.8% of pressures into sacks, dead last among 37 charted passers. His sack rate of 11.9% is 5.2 points above the league average, which works out to a 74-sack pace. All three of his lost fumbles came in the opener. Strip those out and you find a passer whose completion percentage over expected is +1.15, up 3.3 points on last season. He hit 23 of 28 in Cincinnati. The drives died on drop-backs that never became throws: third down at -0.475 EPA, the red zone at -0.548, and the no-huddle at -0.906.

The numbers also hide a game-script split that should worry Tampa. Trailing by nine or more, against softer coverage, he ran at +0.288 EPA with 87% completions. Within one score, which is where most of his football happened, he was at -0.471 with 11 of his 13 sacks. The quick game did not bail him out either. Twenty throws behind the line were all completed and still lost value at -0.264 EPA, so the screen game was not stretching anyone. His bad-throw rate rose every week, from 7.4% to 21.2% to 30.3%. That last game came against Minnesota, now the top-ranked defense, which blitzed him 26 times. That is the one piece of real accuracy erosion in the sample, and it came against the hardest opponent he will see.

Where it goes from here hinges on the thumb and on whether the sack rate returns to his normal, which is bad but survivable. Three games and 118 dropbacks is a small base for a 9-year veteran with a long, ranked track record. The career says the sacks will settle into the high 30s, not the mid 40s. It says the fumbles were a one-game spike and the touchdown rate of 2.1% is far below anything he has posted as a starter. Regression should point up. The ceiling is capped by an offense ranked 31st in pass EPA even with Daniels at quarterback.

strengths.title: Accuracy held up on actual throws
strengths.body: When he got the ball out, it was more accurate than expected: CPOE is positive and well above last year's mark. Most of that came from the short and quick game, where he is completing at a high clip. This fits his 2024 profile and is the most sustainable part of his game if the thumb is sound.

strengths.title: Scrambles still create value
strengths.body: He is still a positive runner, turning scrambles into first downs and positive EPA. He has finished top-10 in QB rushing yards the last two seasons. This is the part of extending plays that pays off, and the career says it is real.

strengths.title: Middle of the field works
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers have been his only clearly positive direction. Chris Godwin Jr. has been his most efficient target per look. Both rest on small samples, 19 attempts and 11 targets, but they point to where the offense should live.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: No charted passer converted more pressures into sacks. That drove the third-down and red-zone collapse. His time to throw rose to 2.99 and his aggressiveness fell, a sign of holding the ball without finding a shot. This is a long-standing trait that spiked, so expect improvement toward his usual rate but not a fix.

concerns.title: Bad throws climbed weekly
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate is up 4.7 points on last year and worsened in each game, peaking at 30.3% against Minnesota's blitz. The context is the league's best defense, but now he returns from a thumb dislocation. Any loss of grip shows up here first.

concerns.title: Close games broke him
concerns.body: Within one score he was badly negative, and nearly all the sacks and both interceptions came there. His good numbers came with Tampa trailing big. The fumbles, all three in week 1, are likely noise. The one-score sack pile-up is the thing that has to change.

trend.note: CPOE dropped from 14 to 4.2 to -14.8 across his three starts, and the bad-throw rate rose each week. The slide ended against the top-ranked defense, then the thumb injury cost him three games.

nextGame.headline: A soft pass rush to return against, if the thumb allows
nextGame.body:
Carolina is close to the ideal opponent for his core flaw. The Panthers rank 27th in hit rate and 21st in sack rate, so the pressure that produced his sack problem should come less often. Their pass defense is 16th by EPA. The catch is that they allow the third-fewest explosive passes, so this sets up as a methodical day rather than a shootout. Their offense ranks 8th and throws far more than the situation predicts. That could keep Tampa in one-score game states, which is exactly where he struggled. A Bucs defense ranked 4th should keep it close.

Availability is the story. Mayfield is listed Out with a dislocated thumb, an estimated return of this game's date, and a report that he was "supposed to practice" Wednesday. Watch the practice reports through the week; a limited week means real rust and grip risk. On the other side, Carolina has lost DT Cam Jackson to injured reserve, which thins an already weak interior rush. The Book makes Tampa a 3.5-point underdog with a 44.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: His sacks vs a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: Carolina rarely hits or sacks quarterbacks, which directly limits his biggest leak. If his pressure-to-sack rate falls back toward his career norm, the drive-killing third downs should ease.

keyMatchups.title: Otton over Egbuka
keyMatchups.body: Carolina has held lead receivers under their averages and been stingy on WR1 targets per play. Tight ends have beaten it, so Cade Otton and the middle of the field look like the path.

keyMatchups.title: Explosives will be scarce
keyMatchups.body: Carolina's defense limits big pass plays, and he completed only 21.4% of deep throws before the injury. Expect a short-to-intermediate game plan rather than shots.

nextGame.watch: Whether he practices fully this week, and then whether his bad-throw rate looks like week 1 or week 3.

restOfSeason.body:
Much of the early damage should regress. The fumbles came in one game. A 44.8% pressure-to-sack rate is well past even his own poor history. A 2.1% touchdown rate is far below every season of his career. If the thumb is healthy, expect something close to his 2025 player: around 205-245 passing yards a game, more touchdowns than his early 0.67 per game, and sacks still above league average. He should keep adding value as a scrambler.

What won't regress is the setting. Tampa's passing offense ranks 31st, and the team is built around a top-5 defense that will play plenty of one-score games. Those are the game states he has struggled in. His 2024 season showed a high ceiling, but that version came with quick, accurate throws and a low aDOT, and the early returns on screens and deep balls don't yet look like it.
swingFactors: Thumb health and grip on returning
Pressure-to-sack rate returning to his career norm
Godwin and Otton carrying the middle of the field

confidence.note: Only three starts, then a thumb dislocation with an uncertain return.
